title: Pockels measures surface films on water
summary: Working at home without university training, Agnes Pockels built a sliding trough to measure surface tension; Lord Rayleigh forwarded her results to Nature in 1891.
why: Helped establish surface science; her trough led to the Langmuir-Blodgett trough.

notes.problem: Source: biography on her 70th birthday in 1932, honorary doctorate 'in the following year' (1933), not 1932. 'Founded' overstates 'fundamental in establishing'.

unsung.contribution: Invented a slide trough for quantitative measurements of surface films on water.
unsung.recognition: She never received a formal appointment for her scientific work; an honorary doctorate came only in 1933.
